name: Tiroler Bergbau- und Hüttenmuseum Brixlegg
kurzbeschreibung: The Mining and Metallurgy Museum in Brixlegg: mining history of the Unterinntal with copper smelting, Fugger heritage, and a rich mineral collection.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Tiroler Bergbau- und H?ttenmuseum is situated in the historic market town of Brixlegg at the entrance to the Alpbachtal valley in the Tyrolean Unterinntal (Kufstein district) at an altitude of approximately 534 metres. Housed in the heritage premises of the former elementary school at R?merstra?e 1, this specialised museum is dedicated to a mining tradition spanning more than 2,000 years: Brixlegg is the oldest copper smelting site in Austria and to this day remains the only secondary copper smelting plant in the Alpine republic. The museum impressively illustrates the rapid rise of the Unterinntal into a global mining economic powerhouse during the Late Middle Ages and the Renaissance.

Copper Smelting, Fugger & Minerals

Archaeological excavations prove that copper ores were already mined and smelted in the Brixlegg region as early as the late Bronze Age, over 3,000 years ago. The site experienced its most glorious era during the 15th and 16th centuries under Archduke Sigmund der M?nzreiche and Emperor Maximilian I., when the prominent Augsburg merchant dynasty of the Fugger took control of the mines and smelting works throughout the Schwaz-Brixlegg region. Across several exhibition floors, the museum documents the entire production chain of historic ore extraction: from arduous miner labour in cramped galleries to the crushing, stamping, and roasting of fahlore, all the way to smelting in ancient reverberatory furnaces. Highlights of the collection include original miners' costumes, historic pit lamps, ancient surveying instruments (Markscheideger?te), guild chests, and intricately engraved smelters' pewter plates. A dedicated section showcases the world-renowned mineral collection: more than 500 exquisite mineral specimens and crystals from Tyrolean deposits ? including azurite, malachite, chalcopyrite, and fahlores ? leave visitors in awe. The exhibition is rounded off by working models of historical smelting furnaces and stamping mills.

Visit & Getting There

The Tiroler Bergbau- und H?ttenmuseum Brixlegg is open from early May to the end of October on Tuesdays and Fridays from 14:00 to 17:00 and on Saturdays from 10:00 to 13:00 (closed on public holidays; group tours available year-round upon advance booking). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. ?6.00, seniors approx. ?5.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. ?3.00, young children free; family ticket approx. ?14.00. Visitors holding the regional Alpbachtal Card receive discounted admission. Getting there by public transport: train (?BB/S-Bahn) to Brixlegg railway station, from where it is just a pleasant five-minute walk to the town centre and R?merstra?e. By car: via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Kramsach/Brixlegg), with free parking available in the town centre of Brixlegg.

Tips

The museum building features low-threshold access via ramps and is designed to accommodate wheelchair users. Following your museum tour, embark on a mining-themed historic walk along the signposted Montanweg Brixlegg-Rattenberg, which passes by historic miners' houses and ancient smelting sites. Afterwards, stop by one of the traditional inns located on Brixlegg's village square.
